cases.name: append_and_pull
cases.note: two devices enrol; A appends; B pulls from cursors; retries are idempotent; gaps and rewrites are seq errors

cases.name: enroll_checks
cases.note: channel binding, household signature, shape, device cap, forgotten devices

cases.name: request_auth
cases.note: unenrolled, unknown channel, stale both ways, bad and cross-verb signatures, junk envelopes, batch and size limits

cases.name: forget_other
cases.note: A appends its Forget op, then records the Forget of B; B's later writes are refused; B reads the channel frozen at the Forget, which holds the Forget op

cases.name: forget_self_handover
cases.note: B records its own Forget before its last ops reach the relay; the ops up to cut_seq still go up, nothing after

cases.name: snapshot_prune
cases.note: a snapshot covering A's first two entries lets them go once retained long enough; a replayed old append stores nothing

cases.name: quotas
cases.note: per-channel bytes, relay-wide bytes, relay-wide channel count

cases.name: rate_limits
cases.note: the device bucket refills one token per interval; the enrol and creation buckets

cases.name: nonce_replay
cases.note: a read's nonce is used once within the window; the same nonce with a new ts is a new request

cases.name: pull_paging
cases.note: a byte budget the first entry may exceed alone, then the entry budget; more is set until the last page

cases.name: list_caps
cases.note: covers and cursors may list at most max_devices uploaders: covers are stored outside the byte quota

cases.name: malformed
cases.note: paths, methods and bodies the handler refuses before any check

cases.name: u64_edges
cases.note: covers and cut_seq above 2^63 - 1 are kept whole and echoed; a cover of 2^64 - 1 covers everything; a batch past 2^64 - 1 is above any cut

cases.name: failed_write_changes_nothing
cases.note: an append refused for quota after pruning leaves the pruned entries in place; the next append that fits prunes them

cases.name: strict_signatures
cases.note: a small-order household key (canonical or not) cannot enrol with a forged auth; an enrolled small-order device key cannot sign

cases.name: labels
cases.note: a label must be NFC (dCBOR text) and 1 to 128 bytes

cases.name: edges
cases.note: only GET /healthz is special; a nonce is live while ts + W >= now

cases.name: epoch_restart
cases.note: reads carry the relay's epoch; a restart keeps the store, empties the nonces, refills the buckets and moves the epoch on, so a read captured before it is refused

cases.name: reader_nonce_cap
cases.note: a reader holds at most max_reader_nonces live nonces; a nonce refused for the cap is not recorded; other readers are unaffected

cases.name: channel_rate
cases.note: the channel bucket is shared by the channel's devices and taken after the device bucket; a channel refusal keeps the device token

cases.name: idle_expiry
cases.note: a channel with no write for idle_ms is expired by the sweep; forgotten records survive it, so a forgotten device cannot enrol again; a channel with none is deleted and frees its slot

cases.name: idle_refresh
cases.note: a repeated enrolment (no ts, replayable) does not keep a channel alive; a retried append (signed, fresh) does; a failed write does not

cases.name: generations
cases.note: enroll and pull name the channel's generation; a restart keeps it; an expired channel kept for its tombstones takes a new one; a deleted channel made again never repeats one
